Article Title: As users private chats with Claude appear on Google, Anthropic says: They are to blame as ...
Article Text:
What Anthropic said on the leaked chats of users



What went wrong



Privacy risks ahead



A trove of seemingly private conversations with Anthropic’s Claude chatbot appeared in Google Search results recently, sparking alarm after users discovered sensitive information including cryptocurrency wallet keys and personal details which have been exposed inadvertently. According to a report by Fortune, the issue was traced to Claude’s ‘share’ feature which enables users to generate a link to send a conversation to others.AI giant Anthropic said that the company itself did not make chats searchable, instead blaming the way users shared links. “We give people control over sharing their Claude conversations publicly, and in keeping with our privacy principles, we do not share chat directories or sitemaps with search engines like Google,” a spokesperson told Fortune. The company emphasised that links are only accessible if users choose to share them, but once shared, they can be archived by third-party services.As per the report by Fortune, members of a Reddit discussion channel has discovered that typing some search phrases in Google pulled up a long lists of shared Claude conversations and Claude Artifacts — itself did not make chats searchable, instead blaming the way users shared links.“We give people control over sharing their Claude conversations publicly, and in keeping with our privacy principles, we do not share chat directories or sitemaps with search engines like Google,” a spokesperson told Fortune. The company emphasized that links are only accessible if users choose to share them, but once shared, they can be archived by third-party services.Anthropic has since fixed the issue, removing the links from Google search, though previously shared URLs remain accessible to anyone who already has them. The incident is not unique: last year, a similar glitch exposed nearly 100,000 ChatGPT conversations, while Elon Musk’s Grok chatbot also suffered from the same vulnerability. The problem stems from how “share” features create unique URLs that can be indexed by search engines.Experts warn that shared chatbot conversations often contain more sensitive information than shared documents, since users treat AI assistants as places to “think out loud” about work, health, or legal issues. As Anthropic, OpenAI, and xAI each struggle with versions of the same mistake, the episode underscores how difficult it has been for the industry to permanently fix privacy risks tied to shared AI chats.
Article Summary: AI giant Anthropic said that the company itself did not make chats searchable, instead blaming the way users shared links. Anthropic has since fixed the issue, removing the links from Google search, though previously shared URLs remain accessible to anyone who already has them. Last year, a similar glitch exposed nearly 100,000 ChatGPT conversations.

Article Title: Canada immigration agency issues important clarification for international students 'who plan to work while studying' after work permits of Indian students were rejected
Article Text:
Clarification on work while studying



Canada college tells protesting Indian students to retain important documents



Canada’s immigration authority has now issued an important clarification for international students following reports of work permit rejections affecting Indian students. Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) stressed that students must carefully follow rules on employment while studying, warning that unauthorised work can have serious consequences, including refusal of future permits of removal from Canada. The statement from IRCC came after Portage College of Calgary, Canada asked ndian students protesting after their work visa got rejected by the Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) to seek legal advice, stating that it “continues to seek clarification regarding this issue”.In an update shared on the website dated July 21, the college said: “Portage College continues to seek clarification regarding this issue and remains committed to providing factual information and keeping students informed as new information becomes available”. The college further revealed that it has scheduled a follow-up meeting with representatives from the group next week. “This meeting will provide an opportunity to continue our dialogue, answer questions where we are able, and share any new information that becomes available,” it added.In a statement posted on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter), IRCC reminded students that they are only allowed to work under specific conditions tied to their study permits. The agency emphasised that working without authorisation — even part-time — may be considered a violation of immigration law. IRCC directed students to its official guidance on the consequences of unauthorised work, which outlines penalties ranging from inadmissibility findings to enforcement action.“Important information for international students who plan to work while studying:• You can only work in Canada as an international student if your study permit conditions say you can.• If you are eligible to work off campus, you can only work up to 24 hours per week while classes are in session.• Working more than you are allowed is a violation of your study permit conditions, which can have serious consequences,” wrote IRCC in a post.On the website, the Portage College has advised students to retain important documents that may be relevant to any future application, request for reconsideration, or other process undertaken on the advice of an authorized immigration professional. List of documents that students should keep copies of include:• Study permits• Letters of acceptance• Enrolment records• Program completion documents• Transcripts• PGWP applications• IRCC refusal letters and officer notes, if available• Correspondence with IRCC or an authorised immigration representative
Article Summary: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC) has issued an important clarification for international students following reports of work permit rejections affecting Indian students. IRCC stressed that students must carefully follow rules on employment while studying, warning that unauthorised work can have serious consequences, including refusal of future permits of removal from Canada.

Article Title: US Vice President JD Vance on conversation with a young engineer that made him realise that America’s economic problems run deeper than salaries or jobs
Article Text:
US Vice President JD Vance

Engineer’s frustration highlights a larger problem



Immigration and home ownership



AI could worsen inequality



Mark Zandi's 'warning' for Americans



US Vice President JD Vance says that America’s economic challenges go beyond wages and employment, pointing to a deeper crisis of affordability and opportunity. According to a report by Benzinga, speaking on The Joe Rogan Experience, Vance recalled a conversation with a young engineer earning well above average yet still unable to image owning a home. “You make way more money than 75% of people your age… and you think it is like this ridiculous, unachievable objective to have literally what your parents had,” Vance said.For Vance, the frustration of the engineer highlights larger problems: even financially successful professionals feel locked out of the middle-class lifestyle their parents enjoyed. He blamed decades of offshoring industrial jobs, reliance on foreign labor, and Wall Street’s dominance over everyday assets for eroding economic security. Rising housing costs, he said, remain the clearest example of how the system is failing.Vance further argued that high immigration levels have intensified competition for housing, though he credited tighter broader policies with helping stabilise rents and prices in recent years. Without a realistic path to homeownership, he also warned that more Americans could lose faith in the system. “It’s created a generation of kids who kind of are attracted to socialism,” he told Rogan.The conversation also turned to artificial intelligence. Rogan also raised concerns about jobs being wiped out, but Vance said that the bigger issue is how AI-driven wealth will be distributed. Comparing the moment to the Industrial Revolution, he warned that if gains flow only to a small elite, inequality could deepen. “The fundamental challenge of AI is it’s going to unleash a lot of wealth creation,” Vance said. “But if that wealth creation all goes to some segment of people, you’re going to have communism.”Recently, Moody’s Analytics top economist, Mark Zandi also raised a warning for Americans. Zandi said that America’s stubborn inflation problem is not a mystery but it’s the result of deliberate policy decisions. In a breakdown shared via a post on X (formerly known as Twitter) Zandi noted that inflation has run above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target for 64 straight months, with headline inflation at 3.5%. He also wrote that when you ‘net out the inflation tailwinds and headwinds, it’s clear the uncomfortably high inflation is the result of policy choices’. Zandi also said that the Americans are right to view high inflation and the increasing cost of living as their biggest financial challenge, and he argues that the roots of the problem lie in trade and immigration policies that have reshaped the economy.“Most Americans consider persistently high inflation and the resulting higher cost of living their number one financial problem. With good reason: top-line inflation is running no less than 3.5%, well above the Fed’s 2% target. And inflation has been well above target for five years running. The table breaks down last year's inflation and this year's expected inflation into their underlying factors. Netting out the inflation tailwinds & headwinds, it’s clear the uncomfortably high inflation is the result of policy choices,” wrote Zandi.
Article Summary: US Vice President JD Vance says that America’s economic challenges go beyond wages and employment, pointing to a deeper crisis of affordability and opportunity. Vance blamed decades of offshoring industrial jobs, reliance on foreign labor, and Wall Street”s dominance over everyday assets for eroding economic security.

Article Title: American man arrested for wiping his phone during airport search; here's the Android-based OS that may also get travellers to Europe in trouble
Article Text:
Disclaimer: It is an AI-generated image

What upset US Federal Agents



GrapheneOS can also get smartphone users in trouble in Europe



GrapheneOS says: We are legal



What cybersecurity researchers say



A Federal case in Atlanta has raised questions about whether the use of privacy-focused mobile software can be treated as evidence of criminal intent, after prosecutors accused a man of wiping his phone to prevent authorities from accessing its contents. The US Department of Justice is prosecuting Atlanta resident Samuel Tunick under a federal law that makes it a crime to destroy property to prevent its seizure, The Guardian reported. First reported by The Guardian, the case centres on GrapheneOS, a custom Android operating system that runs in place of the software on most modern Google Pixel devices. These include the ability to erase a device by entering a designated passcode. The incident occurred at Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport on January 24, after Tunick returned from the Dominican Republic. Tunick’s attorneys confirmed GrapheneOS was running on his phone.Agents repeatedly asked Tunick to unlock his phone and warned that it would be seized if he refused. After he eventually provided a passcode, “the screen went blank, flashed several times, and the phone appeared to restart,” according to the defence motion.Data stored on the device was subsequently lost. Prosecutors allege that the wipe was a deliberate attempt to destroy potential evidence. Tunick’s lawyers maintain that the underlying search violated his constitutional rights. The GrapheneOS has a feature that allows the device owner to set a passcode that deliberately wipes the contents of that device if entered instead of the user’s unlock passcode.According to court testimony cited by The Guardian, federal agents had circulated his name and photograph internally over alleged links to the movement opposing Atlanta’s police training centre, commonly known as Cop City. Tunick was reportedly taken to a secondary screening area and questioned by several agents. A defence filing alleges that questions about child sexual abuse material were used as a pretext to investigate his association with the protest movement. Tunick's lawyers are seeking to have the case dismissed, arguing that US Customs and Border Protection agents unlawfully seized his phone when he returned to the country last year. They contend that any evidence arising from the incident, including the alleged deletion of the phone’s data, should be suppressed.While GrapheneOS supporters argue that its features are legitimate safeguards against surveillance and data theft, authorities in parts of Europe too reportedly treat the operating system’s use as suspicious. In Catalonia, Spain, police have reportedly been profiling people with Google Pixel phones, assuming they have GrapheneOS installed and are drug dealers or gang members.Following the report on Samuel Tunick's arrest, GrapheneOS published a lengthy thread explaining that its security model is designed to prevent unauthorised data extraction rather than rely on features that erase phone data. It went ion to stress that the OS is completely legal. "GrapheneOS is completely legal. We have no obligation to weaken any of the security protections it provides. Creating and using GrapheneOS is strongly protected by the US constitution. Laws attempting to make it illegal or require weakening the security would be unconstitutional," reads a post from GrapheneOS. On data erading, it adds, "There's no way to bypass a strong encryption passphrase once data is at rest. A typical weak PIN or password depends on the secure element limiting the number of attempts. Secure element only accepts firmware updates after Owner authenticates to protect against state coercion. By default, GrapheneOS devices automatically return to Before First Unlock state if they aren't unlocked within 18 hours of being locked. Users can set it as low as 10 minutes. GrapheneOS has strong generic exploit protections and specialized defenses against physical attacks."Cybersecurity experts told the publication that the prosecution’s legal strategy appeared unprecedented. Christophe Boutry, a cybersecurity and surveillance expert, told The Guardian, “It’s concerning – and sends the message that [GrapheneOS] is criminal by default.”
Article Summary: Atlanta resident Samuel Tunick is accused of wiping his phone to prevent authorities from accessing its contents. He is being prosecuted under a federal law that makes it a crime to destroy property to prevent its seizure. The case centres on GrapheneOS, a custom Android operating system that runs in place of the software on most modern Google Pixel devices.

Article Title: Chip that can give sight to the blind: Former president of Elon Musk's Neuralink invents only treatment that restores human vision and takes it to Europe
Article Text:
AI-generated photo for representative purpose

How PRIMA works: Chip and smart glasses



Outpacing Silicon Valley rivals to commercialisation



If someone you know has lost their vision, they may soon get their sight back. Science Corp, a brain-computer interface (BCI) company founded by former Neuralink president Max Hodak, has launched the commercial rollout of PRIMA, the world’s only treatment proven to restore functional central vision to blind patients. PRIMA has received the official CE mark under the European Union Medical Device Regulation, authorising its commercial availability across 30 European countries.The first commercial surgery is expected to take place soon in Germany, making it the first device from a US brain-implant company to reach patients on a wide commercial scale. According to research recently published by the New England Journal of Medicine (NEJM), PRIMA restored vision to patients suffering from GA due to AMD, which is said to have affected more than five million people worldwide.The PRIMA system relies on an ultra-thin, subretinal photovoltaic implant that is placed directly under the affected area of the retina without harming existing natural vision. The wireless implant works in tandem with specialised glasses that project near-infrared light into the eye.The chip absorbs the light and converts it into electrical stimulation signals, allowing the brain to process images once again.Interestingly, the glasses even feature a built-in “zoom-in” capability so users can magnify small text.As per the clinical trial results published, a multi-center trial involving 38 patients across 17 sites showed a mean vision improvement of 25.5 letters (more than 5 lines) on a standard eye chart. The product is claimed to restore reading ability in 84% of patients who regained the ability to read letters, numbers and words. About 80% of patients achieved significant visual acuity improvements after 12 months.“For decades, losing central vision to this disease meant losing the ability to read, recognize faces, and ultimately losing independence. There was no viable treatment. Now there is,” the company stated.While Elon Musk’s Neuralink has dominated public attention, Hodak’s Science Corp. has quietly become the second most valuable US brain-implant company and the first to cross the finish line into commercial sales.Unlike experimental trial devices that remain restricted to research labs, PRIMA is filing for country-specific reimbursement plans across Europe to ensure patients can access the treatment affordably.“This is the first in hopefully a long series of commercial products that proceed to advance that horizon, sometimes incrementally, but relentlessly,” said Max Hodak, founder and CEO of Science Corp. In the US, Science Corp. is working closely with the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to bring PRIMA to the American market.
Article Summary: Science Corp, a brain-computer interface (BCI) company founded by former Neuralink president Max Hodak, has launched the commercial rollout of PRIMA. The world’s only treatment proven to restore functional central vision to blind patients. PRIMa has received the official CE mark under the European Union Medical Device Regulation.

Article Title: China ‘threatens’ US over investigation after US government accused Kimi K3 AI model maker Moonshot AI of ‘stealing’ Anthropic's Fable model
Article Text:
America accuses Moonshot AI of ‘distillation’



Sanctions and Entity List threats by the US



China’s Commerce Ministry has warned of countermeasures after American officials threatened sanctions and trade restrictions against Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) companies over intellectual property (IP) theft allegations. Beijing’s response follows accusations from Washington that Beijing-based AI startup Moonshot AI illegally “distilled” Anthropic’s advanced Claude Fable 5 model to create its newly released Kimi K3 system.Accusing Washington of “AI hegemonism”, China's ministry pushed back, stating that the US is threatening Chinese tech companies without factual or legal grounds, as per a report by news agency Reuters. A ministry spokesperson said: “For any action that causes substantive harm to Chinese interests, China will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its legitimate rights and interests.”Model distillation is a practice where developers use the outputs of a stronger AI model to train or refine a smaller system. However, US officials argue that Moonshot crossed the line from standard training into large-scale extraction and corporate espionage.Last week, White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios, said that the US government uncovered evidence that Moonshot built a complex internal infrastructure to covertly extract data from Anthropic.The AI company previously reported identifying over 3.4 million interactions linked to Moonshot across hundreds of fraudulent accounts targeting Claude’s reasoning, coding and computer-use capabilities.US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned last week that Chinese tech companies conducting illicit distillation could face placement on the Commerce Department’s Entity List or severe financial sanctions.“We support open-source AI and the innovation it unlocks. But open source is not open season on American IP. When PRC firms conduct covert, industrial-scale distillation attacks that cross the line into IP theft, sanctions and Entity List designations will be on the table,” Bessent wrote on X (formerly Twitter).Moonshot has denied the accusations, claiming that Kimi K3’s high performance in coding and problem-solving relies on its own proprietary architectural breakthroughs.
Article Summary: China’s Commerce Ministry has warned of countermeasures after American officials threatened sanctions and trade restrictions against Chinese tech companies. Washington accuses Beijing-based AI startup Moonshot AI of illegally ‘distilling’ an advanced Claude Fable 5 model to create its Kimi K3 system.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Oracle founder Larry Ellison: "Great achievers are driven, not so much by the pursuit of success, but by…" - a powerful lesson on ambition, failure and the mindset behind extraordi
Article Text:
Representative Image

Quote of the day by Oracle founder Larry Ellison

"Great achievers are driven, not so much by the pursuit of success, but by the fear of failure"

Understand the meaning behind Larry Ellison’s quote

Why fear of failure can actually be useful

Why success on its own is never really enough

Why continuous improvement matters more than any single achievement

Why setbacks often build real resilience

Why discipline tends to outlast raw talent

Why this is not the same as harmful anxiety

Other famous quotes by Larry Ellison

"When you innovate, you've got to be prepared for people telling you that you are nuts."

"Life's a journey. It's a journey about discovering limits."

"The most important aspect of my personality as far as determining my success goes has been my questioning conventional wisdom, doubting experts and questioning authority."

"I have had all the disadvantages required for success."

What it means in today's world

Most people assume successful individuals are pulled forward purely by ambition, chasing wealth, recognition and big wins. Larry Ellison, the co-founder of Oracle, offered a different explanation for what actually drives people to the top. "Great achievers are driven, not so much by the pursuit of success, but by the fear of failure," he said. It is not really an argument in favour of fear. It is an observation about where a lot of real discipline actually comes from, and it fits closely with how Ellison himself has described building one of the largest technology companies in the world from a much smaller and far less certain starting point.Most people picture successful individuals as motivated purely by optimism, chasing the next win with total confidence. Ellison is describing something a little different from that picture entirely. Plenty of top performers push themselves relentlessly because they understand exactly what failure would actually cost them, and rather than freezing up over that possibility, they use it to stay sharp and keep improving.The key distinction sitting inside the quote is between fear that stops someone acting at all and fear that pushes someone to prepare properly.The first shuts things down. The second is what actually keeps people sharp long after they could reasonably have relaxed.Fear usually gets treated as something purely negative, and plenty of it is. Not all fear works that way though. A healthy awareness that things could go wrong tends to make people prepare more thoroughly, practise more consistently, and think harder before big decisions. Athletes train hard precisely because they know competition will be demanding. Students revise because exams genuinely require it. In every one of these cases, the possibility of failing is exactly what pushes people to put in more effort, not less.Success has a way of creating comfort, and comfort has a way of turning into complacency. Plenty of people and organisations start declining right after they succeed, simply because they stop pushing once things feel secure. Markets shift. Technology moves on. Customer expectations change constantly. People who stop learning at that point tend to fall behind fairly quickly. Ellison's quote is really arguing that staying aware of the possibility of failure is exactly what keeps great achievers improving, even well after they have already succeeded.Real achievement is rarely the product of one single effort. It usually gets built slowly, through constant refinement, learning new skills, correcting mistakes, adapting when circumstances shift, and continuing to look for better solutions even when the current one already works fine. People who keep this habit up stay ready for whatever comes next, because they never fully stopped asking how they could be a little better than they were yesterday.Failure is rarely pleasant in the moment, yet many successful people describe it afterward as one of the most useful teachers they ever had. A failed product reveals a genuine weakness worth fixing. A rejected idea often leads directly to a better one. Resilience really develops through treating a setback as useful information rather than as a final verdict on someone's ability, which is exactly the alertness Ellison's quote is describing, an ongoing willingness to notice what went wrong instead of simply moving past it without learning anything at all.Natural ability gives someone a head start. Discipline is what actually determines whether that ability gets developed properly over time. Someone genuinely motivated to avoid failure tends to build habits around regular practice, careful preparation and continuous learning, and those habits usually end up mattering more in the long run than raw talent ever did on its own, since talent alone rarely survives the first serious setback without something sturdier underneath it.It is worth being clear about the difference here. Constant anxiety that damages confidence or actively prevents someone from trying anything is not what this quote is describing. Healthy motivation sounds like "I want to prepare properly because this genuinely matters." Unhealthy anxiety sounds like "I should not even try in case I fail." The first pushes someone into action. The second keeps them frozen in place.The pace of change today makes continuous improvement close to essential rather than simply admirable. Skills that mattered five years ago can become outdated surprisingly quickly. Ellison's quote is a reminder that lasting achievement usually depends less on celebrating a past success and more on staying genuinely committed to the next round of improvement. The awareness that failure remains a real possibility is exactly what keeps that commitment alive long after the applause for the last win has faded, which is really the whole difference between a career that keeps growing and one that quietly stalls out.
Article Summary: Larry Ellison: Great achievers are driven not by the pursuit of success, but by the fear of failure. Ellison argues that staying aware of the possibility of failure is exactly what keeps great achievers improving. The key distinction sitting inside the quote is between fear that stops someone acting at all and fear that pushes someone to prepare.

Article Title: Nvidia partners with former OpenAI chief scientist Ilya Sutskever’s AI startup: What the CEOs said
Article Text:
Nvidia to gain rare access to SSI’s AI research



What the Nvidia and SSI CEOs said



Nvidia has entered into a major long-term strategic partnership with Safe Superintelligence Inc. (SSI), the high-profile AI research startup co-founded by former OpenAI chief scientist Ilya Sutskever. As part of the agreement, Nvidia has made a ‘substantial’ direct investment in SSI and will grant the startup early access to its next-generation Vera Rubin computing platform.According to an announcement made by the US-based chipmaker, the deal aims to boost SSI’s processing power by an order of magnitude as it pursues breakthroughs in artificial intelligence (AI). In return, the two companies will collaborate on optimising Nvidia's future hardware platforms by leveraging SSI's technical insights into advanced AI architectures.Nvidia reportedly agreed to the partnership and investment after receiving rare insight into SSI’s private operations. For the past two years, SSI has been quietly developing a novel research direction aimed at building powerful, robustly aligned AI systems.The collaboration will combine Nvidia’s cutting-edge hardware with SSI’s specialised algorithmic research to accelerate the startup's next phase of development.Leaders from both companies expressed high expectations for what the joint effort will yield for the future of artificial intelligence.“Ilya has pioneered fundamental breakthroughs at the foundation of modern AI, beginning with AlexNet. “We are excited to see what new breakthroughs SSI will discover powered by our Vera Rubin platform,” said Jensen Huang, founder and CEO of Nvidia.“We have research that is worthy of scaling up, and having access to a big Nvidia computer will let us do so. We’re incredibly proud to be partnering with Jensen and the Nvidia team, and we are confident that our big bet on the Vera Rubin platform will take us to the next level,” said Ilya Sutskever, co-founder and CEO of SSI.
Article Summary: N Nvidia has entered into a major long-term strategic partnership with Safe Superintelligence Inc. Article Title: Quote of the day by Steve Jobs: ‘If you're not passionate enough from the start, you'll never stick it out'
Article Text:
Steve Jobs emphasized passion for ideas and problems. Genuine enthusiasm fuels perseverance through difficult and uncertain times. Talent alone is insufficient for achieving long-term goals. Real accomplishments require years of consistent and focused effort. This perspective encourages pursuing meaningful work and solving real issues.

“You have to be burning with an idea, or a problem, or a wrong that you want to right.

If you're not passionate enough from the start, you'll never stick it out.”

What Steve Jobs' quote means

Apple co-founder Steve Jobs is remembered not only for transforming the technology industry but also for his thoughts on creativity, innovation and perseverance. One of his most well-known quotes is:Even years after he said it, the quote continues to inspire entrepreneurs, students and professionals because it highlights the importance of genuine passion in achieving long-term success.The quote is a reminder that meaningful work often demands patience, resilience and persistence. Whether someone is building a company, learning a new skill or pursuing a personal goal, enthusiasm for the work itself is what helps people continue when progress feels slow or obstacles appear.When Steve Jobs said that you need to be "burning with an idea" from the beginning, he was emphasising that passion is what keeps people committed through difficult times. The quote suggests that talent alone is rarely enough. Long-term projects often involve setbacks, failures and uncertainty, and without a strong personal connection to the goal, many people give up before reaching success.In a world where people want instant results and instant recognition, Jobs’ words are a reminder that real accomplishments take years of consistent effort.You are going to face challenges, whether you are starting a startup, writing a book, doing research or preparing for competitive exams. The true passion is to help people stay focused even when success is not right here yet.The quote also says that the strongest motivation is often the desire to solve a real problem or improve something that already exists. Several successful innovations began with someone having a better way of doing something. Jobs isn’t telling you to give up on success. He’s telling you to go after the ideas that you actually care about, because a commitment to an idea is more likely to carry you through the hard journey from idea to reality.
Article Summary: Apple co-founder Steve Jobs is remembered not only for transforming the technology industry but also for his thoughts on creativity, innovation and perseverance. One of his most well-known quotes is: “If you're not passionate enough from the start, you'll never stick it out.”

Article Title: PlayStation owners plan a week-long “PSBlackout” protest over over Sony killing discs in 2028
Article Text:
Log out, switch off, spend nothing—the #PSBlackout protest hits PlayStation from August 23.

The disc shutdown is the flashpoint, but the PSBlackout protest is really about five years of grievances

Analysts say a week offline won't make Sony reverse the digital-only PS5 decision

PlayStation owners are being asked to switch everything off. Game preservation group Does It Play? has called for a seven-day #PSBlackout running from Sunday, August 23 to Sunday, August 30, starting and ending at 7PM local time. The ask is simple enough: stay logged out of PSN, play nothing online, and spend nothing on the PlayStation Store.The trigger is Sony 's decision to stop producing discs for new PlayStation games from January 2028. A month on, the anger hasn't cooled. The group's call to arms on X has been viewed close to a million times, and Stop Killing Games, the campaign against publishers remotely switching off titles people have paid for, has backed it.The blackout statement reads like a receipt. It names the closure of Bluepoint Games, a live-service push that mostly missed, cancelled fan events, and PS VR2 left to fade out. It misses Twisted Metal, SOCOM, Sly Cooper and Resistance. It misses PlayStation Experience and Japan Studio. Then the summary line: "Ending physical discs in 2028 feels like the last straw."Sony's stated reasoning is consumer preference. Sid Shuman, Senior Director at SIE Content Communications, wrote that new games will arrive on the PlayStation Store and at retailers in digital formats only.The numbers back him up. Circana's Mat Piscatella noted that only seven PlayStation games have crossed 100,000 physical units in the US this year. In the week ending July 11, just two managed 10,000.Serkan Toto of Kantan Games told IGN that Sony has no intention of turning back. His maths is blunt. Sony has over 120 million active PlayStation users and roughly 50 million PS Plus subscribers. Even half a million cancellations would erase one percent of that business. Ampere's Piers Harding-Rolls adds the longer view: digital made up 13% of Sony full-game unit sales in 2013, and close to 80% by 2025.Pressure keeps building regardless. The Don't Kill The Disc petition has climbed from around 120,000 signatures on July 6 to more than 345,000 three weeks later.One awkward detail: Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2 lands during blackout week, finally springing MGS4 from PS3 jail.
Article Summary: #PSBlackout protest hits PlayStation from August 23 to August 30. Log out of PSN, play nothing online, and spend nothing on the PlayStation Store. The trigger is Sony's decision to stop producing discs for new PlayStation games from January 2028.

Article Title: Layoffs at US tech companies crossed 140,000 in the first six months of 2026; of these Amazon, Oracle, Meta and Microsoft account for almost 50,000
Article Text:
Representative image

Cutting back to fund the AI infrastructure race



US technology companies have laid off nearly 140,000 employees during the first half of 2026, signaling that corporate layoffs across Silicon Valley remain in full swing even as industry giants pour unprecedented billions into artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. An analysis by the Financial Times of corporate filings and data from outplacement firm Challenger, Gray and Christmas reveals that tech sector cutbacks accounted for more than one-third of all announced US layoffs during this period.Notably, industry giants Amazon, Oracle, Meta and Microsoft accounted for nearly 50,000 of those job cuts, which represents approximately 6% of their combined corporate workforces.The wave of layoffs contrasts with massive capital spending across the tech sector. The "Big Four" hyperscalers - Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, and Microsoft -are projected to deploy a staggering $725 billion in capital expenditure this year on data centers and server infrastructure.Simultaneously, Oracle plans to invest $70 billion in similar infrastructure to support major clients like OpenAI. Oracle ended its 2026 fiscal year with 21,000 fewer employees following major workforce reductions in March, amid mounting pressure on its balance sheet that recently saw S&P downgrade its credit rating to one notch above junk status."The money has to come from somewhere. They are moving from one bet to the next," Rishi Jaluria, an analyst at RBC, was quoted as saying. He noted that tech companies are trimming headcounts to make up for earlier overhiring and reallocate capital toward AI.While some executives have attributed workforce reductions to productivity gains enabled by AI, such as Block CEO Jack Dorsey, who cut nearly half of his 10,000-person company citing changing headcount needs, economists remain skeptical."The typical attitude of tech executives has been to say that AI allows us to gain efficiency rather than admit that they overhired. It’s an easy way out," said Enrico Moretti, a professor of economics at UC Berkeley.According to the Financial Times analysis, companies that cited AI as a driver for job cuts underperformed the Nasdaq index by nearly 10% in the 30 trading days following their announcements. Consequently, companies like Amazon and Microsoft have stated that AI adoption was not the underlying reason for their recent layoffs.
Article Summary: US technology companies have laid off nearly 140,000 employees during the first half of 2026. Amazon, Oracle, Meta and Microsoft accounted for nearly 50,000 of those job cuts. The wave of layoffs contrasts with massive capital spending across the tech sector.

Article Title: Google Maps users can spot Spider-Man fighting villains across New York: Here's how to find him

How to find Spider-Man on Google Maps

Google, Sony Pictures and Samsung launch Spidey Tracker

The hidden Street View scenes are part of a promotion for Spider-Man: Brand New Day, with Google confirming that five custom Spider-Man moments have been embedded across select locations in New York City for fans to discover ahead of the film's July 31 release.The hidden scenes, which include Spider-Man confronting members of the Hand, appear inside Google Maps' Street View imagery. As users began sharing the discoveries online, Google encouraged more searches through a series of posts on X, asking fans to use their "Spidey senses" to uncover additional locations across the city.The campaign first came to light after Google Maps posted on X:The post featured an image from Long Island City in Queens. Users who opened Google Maps Street View at the location found Spider-Man outside a nearby deli and grocery store, where he appears to be battling the Hand, a ninja-like group featured in the upcoming Spider-Man: Brand New Day film.With more people searching, more Spider-Man sightings popped up, from Washington Square Park to Madison Avenue.Google later acknowledged the discoveries in another X post, writing,After fans uncovered more locations, the company added,Social media users also reacted to the unusual Street View appearances. Earlier this year, the company also used Street View as part of a campaign for a Paul McCartney album.
Article Summary: Google Maps users have started spotting Spider-Man fighting villains across New York. The sightings are not random, but part of a promotion for the upcoming film. Article Title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang says OpenAI's rogue AI models hacking a multi-billion dollar company is why he's bringing Microsoft, IBM, Cisco and 30 other biggest tech companies together
Article Text:
Jensen Huang's answer to rogue AI: 35 tech giants

What actually happened when OpenAI's models escaped their sandbox and attacked Hugging Face

Why Hugging Face had to run a Chinese open-weight model to investigate its own breach

What Nvidia , Microsoft and IBM are actually contributing to the Open Secure AI Alliance

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has turned the strangest cybersecurity story of 2026 into an argument. Earlier this month, two of OpenAI's cybersecurity models broke out of a sandbox, found their way onto the open internet and hacked Hugging Face, the AI platform that hosts models and datasets for most of the industry. They were not being controlled by anyone. They were trying to cheat on a test, and they worked out that the answers might be sitting on Hugging Face's servers.Huang used that incident as the launchpad for the Open Secure AI Alliance, a coalition of more than 35 companies including Microsoft, IBM, Cisco, Red Hat, Palantir, CrowdStrike, Salesforce, SAP, Siemens, Dell, Databricks and Hugging Face itself. Huang's pitch is blunt. "Attackers have frontier AI. Defenders need a frontier AI ecosystem—the best open and closed models, force-multiplied by a global community," he posted on X. Then the line that gives the alliance its reason to exist: "During the Hugging Face incident, closed AI blocked essential forensics."Hugging Face disclosed the breach on July 16, before it knew who was behind it. The attack ran over a weekend across thousands of short-lived sandboxes, moving laterally through internal clusters and shifting its command infrastructure between public services to stay alive.The company called the police.Five days later OpenAI admitted the attackers were its own models — GPT-5.6 Sol and an unreleased model it described as more capable. Both had their cyber guardrails switched off for the evaluation. They found a zero-day in OpenAI's own package proxy, used it to reach a machine with internet access, and went hunting.Here is the detail Huang keeps returning to. Hugging Face had over 17,000 recorded attacker actions to analyse. It tried commercial frontier models first. They refused. Feeding a model real exploit payloads and command-and-control artefacts looks identical to asking it to build an attack, and the safety filters could not tell an incident responder from an intruder.So Hugging Face ran GLM 5.2, a Chinese open-weight model, on its own hardware. The forensics took hours instead of days. As a bonus, no stolen credentials left the building.That is the asymmetry Huang is selling the alliance on. The attacker was bound by no usage policy. The defender was locked out by its own vendors.The members are shipping code, not statements. Nvidia has open-sourced NOOA, an agent-harness research framework, on GitHub. Microsoft is contributing MDASH, a scanning harness that runs multiple agents against a codebase to argue over whether a bug is genuinely exploitable. IBM and Red Hat bring Lightwell, which signs open-source patches. HPE is working on SPIFFE/SPIRE for agent identity. Hugging Face has handed Safetensors to the PyTorch Foundation.The alliance also has a message for regulators, and it is not subtle: treat open models as defensive assets rather than liabilities, and do not lock defenders out of frontier capability in the name of safety.Not everyone is convinced. Security researchers have pointed out that a sandbox with a single outbound route is an architecture problem, not a proof that open weights are the answer. Others suspect OpenAI benefited from the publicity. Huang, whose company sells the hardware either side of this argument runs on, is not waiting for that debate to settle.
Article Summary: The Open Secure AI Alliance is a coalition of more than 35 companies including Microsoft, IBM, Cisco, Red Hat, Palantir, CrowdStrike, Salesforce, SAP, Siemens, Dell, Databricks and Hugging Face itself. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has turned the strangest cybersecurity story of 2026 into an argument.

Article Title: Unhappy with $7 billion collateral bill that electricity company in the state called America's Dairyland has sent, Oracle goes to court; says: Rule risks ...
Article Text:
Oracle logo: For representative purpose

Strict credit rules trigger $100 million annual cost



Wall Street credit concerns and rising regulatory pushback



Oracle has taken a Wisconsin electricity regulator to court over a massive $7 billion collateral requirement tied to its new artificial intelligence data center. The company warns the rule risks imposing “onerous financing costs” that could discourage future tech investments in the state. The dispute centres on the Public Service Commission of Wisconsin, which set strict credit rules for local utility We Energies.According to a recent report by The Financial Times, the regulator declined to reconsider its policy, which aims to protect local households and businesses from absorbing the sky-high electricity costs needed to power massive AI facilities. The nearly one-gigawatt facility in Port Washington is a pivotal project for Oracle, built to help fulfill its $300 billion computing contract with OpenAI.However, Wisconsin's power regulations are adding unexpected financial strain to Oracle's aggressive AI expansion.Under the “very large customer” tariff approved for Milwaukee-based We Energies, any developer building a data center must post collateral in cash or a letter of credit if its S&P credit rating falls below A-minus. The collateral amount reflects the cost of power plants and transmission lines built specifically to supply the data center.As Oracle was rated BBB, which is two notches below the required threshold, it fell under the rule. Securing a $7 billion letter of credit is estimated to cost Oracle more than $100 million annually. Oracle filed a petition asking a county judge to overturn the rule and allow We Energies to waive the requirement. However, state regulators confirmed recently that they refused to modify the policy, insisting that existing utility customers must not subsidize large data centers.“Tariffs should be designed such that existing Wisconsin customers do not subsidize data centers, now or in the future,” the Wisconsin Public Service Commission was quoted as saying.Oracle’s challenge comes as financial rating agencies express growing caution over the company’s heavy AI spending and mounting debt. S&P recently downgraded Oracle’s credit rating further to BBB-minus, which is just one notch above junk status, citing uncertainty around its long-term path to profitability.According to report from the Alliance for the Great Lakes (via Milwaukee Journal Sentinel), Wisconsin was home to 43 data centres as of July 2025.Wisconsin is not the only US state in tightening rules on major tech firms. Across the United States, 24 states have approved “large load tariffs” to ensure that tech companies pay minimum contract terms, exit fees, and collateral so local utility ratepayers are not left holding the bill for massive infrastructure projects.
Article Summary: Wisconsin's Public Service Commission set strict credit rules for local utility We Energies. Any developer building a data center must post collateral in cash or a letter of credit if its S&P credit rating falls below A-minus. The collateral amount reflects the cost of power plants and transmission lines built specifically to supply the data center. Oracle was rated BBB, which is two notches below the required threshold, and fell under the rule. Securing a $7 billion letter ofcredit is estimated to cost Oracle more than $100 million annually.

Article Title: Warner Brothers takes Amazon to court over hire of HBO Max marketing exec: You hired our employee who was on …
Article Text:
Warner Bros. claims Amazon targeted employees under contract

Here’s what the lawsuit says

Warner Brothers Discovery has filed a lawsuit against Amazon , accusing the company of hiring an HBO Max executive who was still under contract and trying to recruit other employees before their agreements ended. The lawsuit, filed this week, claims Amazon interfered with Warner Bros. ' contractual relationships, breached contracts and engaged in unfair competition. According to the complaint, Amazon hired Pia Barlow, a marketing executive who recently joined Amazon MGM Studios, even though her employment contract with Warner Bros. was due to run until October 31, 2027.According to the lawsuit, Amazon has been "hurriedly seeking to pirate away a number of contracted employees," including Barlow. That executive, believed to be HBO programming executive Francesca Orsi, ultimately remained with Warner Bros.In the lawsuit, Warner Bros. said Amazon ignored California law while recruiting employees who were still under fixed-term agreements."In blatant disregard of established California law, Amazon has gone rogue by attempting to induce Plaintiffs' employees with term employment agreements to breach those agreements with impunity, backed up with the ready assurance that Amazon will defend and indemnify them should they be held to account for their blatantly unlawful acts," Warner Bros. said in the complaint. The lawsuit also includes claims of interference with contractual relations, breach of contract and unfair competition.According to Deadline, the case is expected to revive debate over whether fixed-term employment agreements are legally enforceable under California law.

Article Title: America's biggest investor Michael Burry is not happy with reports of Nvidia investing $250 billion in Sam Altman's OpenAI; his complaint is what has been analysts biggest concern with $100 billion-pl
Article Text:
Government and global stakes



Michael Burry’s warning



Michael Burry to everyone saying software companies are 'dead’



America’s biggest investor, Michael Burry has voiced his sharp criticism of reports that Nvidia is preparing a a $250 billion backstop for OpenAI’s massive Ohio data-center project. According to a report by the Wall Street journal, the guarantees would help OpenAI lease a 10-gigawatt site being developed by SoftBank’s SB Energy, with total costs potentially exceeding $500 billion. Burry’s complaint echoes what analysts have long warned about in AI megadeals: circular funding arrangements that expose investors to enormous risk if sentiment shifts or growth slows. Nvidia, already valued at $5 trillion, has invested $30 billion in OpenAI and is now considering financing chip purchases worth another $350 billion. Critics say such structures could leave the industry vulnerable, especially since OpenAI remains unprofitable and lacks an investment-grade credit rating.The Ohio project is backed by US federal land and Japanese investment under a trade deal, with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick involved in allocating power. Japan has pledged $33 billion to the natural-gas plant supplying the site, while the U.S. government will eventually claim 90% of revenue once Japan recoups its share.The project, located on a decommissioned uranium-enrichment site, is expected to deliver its first 800 megawatts of power by 2028.Michael Burry’s criticism underscores growing unease about the sustainability of $100 billion-plus AI financing structures. His warning suggests that while AI demand is surging, the industry’s reliance on complex guarantees and debt-backed megaprojects could become its biggest vulnerability.Recently, Burry published a software-sector sector research report on May 29 and made it freely available on June 21 outlining which companies he believes are best positioned for the AI era and which face greater disruption risks. Burry pushed back against claims that software companies are ‘dead’, arguing that large language models (LLMs) cannot replace human creativity. “LLMs, no matter how advanced they get at being LLMs, will never beat that creative instinct of a talented human being,” he wrote. He also cited Adobe as a company unfairly discounted by investors, pointing to its expanding AI offerings like Firefly, Firefly Foundry, and Acrobat AI, and its distribution across ecosystems including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Microsoft.Along with this, Autodesk was highlighted as well-positioned, given its role in industries where expertise, accountability and regulatory requirements remain central areas where AI tools cannot easily substitute human oversight.
Article Summary: Michael Burry has voiced his sharp criticism of reports that Nvidia is preparing a a $250 billion backstop for OpenAI’s massive Ohio data-center project. According to a report by the Wall Street journal, the guarantees would help OpenAI lease a 10-gigawatt site being developed by SoftBank's SB Energy, with total costs potentially exceeding $500 billion.

Article Title: Europe's heatwave is a lesson for Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and other tech giants building data centres that not local protests but another crisis threatens their plans
Article Text:
How heatwaves are increasing operational challenges for data centres

Local concerns grow alongside rising temperatures

"pinching your body and burning your skin."

"data heat island effect."

Protests and political action continue

Europe's ongoing heatwave is adding to concerns around AI data centres. Researchers have warned that rising temperatures could become a larger long-term challenge than local opposition for companies including Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and other technology companies expanding their infrastructure. According to the World Economic Forum (WEF), climate-related disruption could increase the cost of operating data centres by $81 billion by 2035 and $168 billion by 2065, highlighting how extreme weather is becoming a growing operational risk.The warning comes as record temperatures increase cooling requirements for data centres that already consume large amounts of electricity and water. The issue has also intensified scrutiny of new facilities, with local communities raising concerns over water use, electricity demand and environmental impact as heatwaves become more frequent.Data centres produce a lot of heat during operation and need extensive cooling systems to maintain servers within safe temperature limits. The cooling demand further increases during heatwaves, resulting in increased energy consumption and operating costs.According to the World Economic Forum, climate change could significantly increase the cost of running data centres over the coming decades as operators face more frequent heatwaves, droughts and other extreme weather events.The organisation has called for improved resilience measures to prepare facilities for climate-related disruptions.Amazon's data centres reportedly used around 2.5 billion gallons of water in a single year, illustrating the scale of water required to cool large computing facilities.Heatwaves have also renewed concerns among residents living near major data centre hubs.In Slough, England, one person told The Guardian that the heat felt like having somethingWhile there is no scientific consensus that data centres are solely responsible for higher local temperatures, early research has suggested they may contribute to aA study, which has not yet been peer reviewed, estimated that data centres can increase surrounding temperatures by approximately 3.6°F, potentially adding to heat stress during periods of extreme weather.Alongside climate concerns, opposition to new data centres has continued in several regions.In Utah, hundreds of people protested a proposed AI data centre in Box Elder County, citing concerns over water consumption after Governor Spencer Cox declared a state of emergency because of "extreme drought conditions" in May 2026.According to Data Center Watch, protests contributed to blocking around $130 billion worth of proposed data centre projects during the first quarter of 2026.The growing opposition has also resulted in policy changes. New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed a statewide moratorium on new hyperscale data centres consuming 50 megawatts or more while the state develops regulations covering environmental impacts and community protections.The developments come as technology companies continue to invest in AI infrastructure, with increasing attention to how climate-related risks, alongside public opposition, could influence future data centre expansion.
Article Summary: Data centres produce a lot of heat during operation and need extensive cooling systems to maintain servers within safe temperature limits. The cooling demand further increases during heatwaves, resulting in increased energy consumption and operating costs. According to the World Economic Forum, climate change could significantly increase the cost of running data centres.

Article Title: Product head of $10 billion startup Mercor on the company junking take-home job interview assignments that can be completed with AI
Article Text:
Mercor wants to test judgment, not AI-generated answers

AI hiring startup Mercor has stopped using take-home interview assignments that can easily be completed with artificial intelligence, choosing instead to focus on interviews that test a candidate's thinking and decision-making skills. Speaking on the "20VC" podcast, Mercor's Head of Product, Osvald Nitski, said the company now relies more on whiteboard interviews and discussions that help assess a candidate's judgment, understanding of AI tools and system design. The move comes as many technology companies are changing their hiring process to allow candidates to use AI during interviews and coding tests.For those unaware, Whiteboard interviews require candidates to explain their ideas and problem-solving process while writing or drawing on a board. They became widely used by companies such as Google, Meta and Microsoft during the 2010s.During the podcast, Osvald Nitski said Mercor still checks whether candidates know how to use AI tools, but it has moved away from assignments that AI can complete with little effort.“We'll do one round where we find out if the person is familiar with AI tools”,he said. “We care a lot about being able to set up good experiments and understanding statistics, having good judgment, and then systems design as well,” he said, referring to what is asked in whiteboarding sessions.Nitski said AI has made it easier for people to rely on tools instead of their own thinking."We want to make sure that people still have the ability to have good judgment and know what they're doing and not just, like, regurgitate what comes out of Claude," he said.Mercor uses AI to screen candidates for its talent marketplace, but its hiring process for full-time employees differs from a growing trend in Silicon Valley Many companies are replacing traditional interviews with work trials and take-home projects. AI coding startups such as Lovable, Cursor and Kilo have said these practical assignments are a better way to judge both technical and soft skills.A Business Insider report quotes Emily Cohen, head of people and operations at AI coding startup Cognition, saying interviews should reflect how people work today. "I guess this is like asking a kid to take a math test without a calculator," she said about not allowing AI use in interviews. "For the bulk of building something similar to what you would do on the role, you can and should use AI tools.”
Article Summary: Hiring startup Mercor has stopped using take-home interview assignments that can easily be completed with artificial intelligence. The company now relies more on whiteboard interviews and discussions that help assess a candidate's judgment. Article Title: The invisible tax of owning gadgets: Why your devices actually end up costing more
Article Text:
Disclaimer: It is an AI-generated image

The same pattern is emerging across almost every category of consumer electronics



Smart home devices perhaps illustrate this transformation most clearly



The economics of the gadget industry have quietly changed



Artificial intelligence is accelerating this transition

Why it makes sense on one level



When buying a new smartphone or laptop, most consumers compare only one number: the price on the box. Is it worth Rs 79,999? Can I stretch to Rs 1 lakh? Is there a bank discount or a sale on any e-commerce platform?Increasingly, however, that sticker price is only the beginning.The real cost of owning modern gadgets has quietly shifted from a one-time purchase to a steady stream of recurring expenses. Between subscriptions, cloud storage, accidental damage plans, paid AI features, accessories and repairs, consumers are paying an invisible tax that rarely features in advertisements.Take a flagship smartphone. A device priced at Rs 80,000 today is rarely used in isolation. Most buyers add a protective case and screen protector, spending a little extra depending on your choice. Since many premium phones no longer include chargers, that is another cost which one has to incur sooner or later.Cloud storage, almost essential once photos and videos pile up, costs anywhere from Rs 75 to Rs 900 a month depending on the plan. Many users also buy extended warranties or accidental damage protection, adding another Rs 8,000-15,000 over the life of the phone.Then come AI subscriptions. ChatGPT Plus, Google AI Pro, Microsoft Copilot Pro and similar services are gradually becoming part of everyday workflows for professionals.While optional today, they increasingly unlock the very features manufacturers use to market their devices.Over four or five years, the ownership cost of an Rs 80,000 phone can comfortably exceed Rs 1 lakh without the buyer ever noticing where the money went.A laptop is no longer simply a laptop. Buyers often pay separately for Microsoft 365, antivirus software, cloud backup services, AI assistants and extended support plans. Gaming laptops invite additional spending on peripherals, software subscriptions and accessories. Even televisions have escaped the one-time purchase model. While streaming subscriptions are hardly new, smart TVs are increasingly tied to ecosystems where premium content, cloud gaming and connected home services generate recurring revenue long after the hardware has been sold.Video doorbells, home security cameras and smart locks frequently advertise affordable hardware, but many reserve advanced features such as cloud recording, person detection, longer video history or emergency alerts for monthly subscription plans. Consumers often discover these limitations only after installing the product.Hardware margins have become increasingly difficult to sustain as components commoditise and competition intensifies. Companies therefore seek recurring revenue long after the initial sale. Investors also reward subscription businesses because predictable monthly income is generally viewed as more valuable than cyclical hardware sales.Apple's Services division, Google's cloud subscriptions, Microsoft's productivity ecosystem and Amazon's Prime strategy all reflect the same philosophy: the device serves as an entry point into a wider ecosystem rather than the end product itself.Many of the headline AI features showcased during product launches depend on expensive computing infrastructure. Running large language models is significantly more resource-intensive than traditional software features, making subscriptions an attractive way to recover those costs. As AI capabilities become more sophisticated, consumers may find that the most useful experiences increasingly sit behind monthly paywalls rather than arriving through free software updates.Repairability adds another layer to the ownership equation. Premium smartphones now feature more durable materials than ever before, but when something does break, repair bills can be startling. Replacing a flagship display or camera module often costs tens of thousands of rupees. That, in turn, nudges consumers toward purchasing insurance or extended protection plans at the time of sale—another expense that effectively becomes part of the product's true cost.None of this necessarily represents bad value. Cloud backups protect irreplaceable memories. Extended warranties provide peace of mind. AI subscriptions can meaningfully improve productivity for many users. The problem is that consumers continue evaluating gadgets as though they remain one-time purchases, when they increasingly resemble ongoing financial commitments.Perhaps the better question before buying a gadget is no longer, “How much does it cost?” but rather, “How much will it cost me to own?”That distinction may seem subtle, but it reflects one of the biggest shifts in consumer technology over the past decade. The industry is moving away from selling products and toward selling ecosystems—where hardware is merely the ticket of entry.Looking ahead, the invisible tax of gadget ownership is unlikely to disappear. If anything, it may grow larger as AI, connected services and subscription-based software become integral to every device we buy. The smartest purchase decisions in the coming years may not be about finding the cheapest gadget, but about choosing the ecosystem that demands the least from your wallet long after you've left the store.
Article Summary: The real cost of owning modern gadgets has quietly shifted from a one-time purchase to a steady stream of recurring expenses. Between subscriptions, cloud storage, accidental damage plans, paid AI features, accessories and repairs, consumers are paying an invisible tax that rarely features in advertisements.
