Article Title: Google AI CEO Demis Hassabis on why DeepMind sold to Google: The Atari work alerted the Silicon Valley, and they came after my people
Article Text:
Demis Hassabis sold DeepMind to Google in 2014

Demis Hassabis had no product and no revenue when Google, Facebook and Musk started circling DeepMind



Demis Hassabis has given the plainest account yet of why he sold DeepMind to Google in 2014, and it has nothing to do with grand strategy. It was arithmetic. He reckoned that staying in the fight against the biggest technology companies in the world would take roughly $7 billion. At the time, he says, he was struggling to close rounds a fraction of that size. "The reason I sold was I knew it would require 7 billion dollars of investment," he said, adding that he "was barely able to scrape together 10 million dollar rounds at that point."The trigger, by his telling, was Atari. DeepMind's agents had learned to play classic arcade games from raw pixels alone, with nobody explaining the rules. It was a research result, not a product. But it was enough to turn a small London lab into a name that people in Mountain View and Menlo Park started saying out loud. "We'd done enough, the Atari thing, we had alerted enough of the Silicon Valley titans," Hassabis said. "They were coming after my people."DeepMind had nothing to defend itself with. No revenue, no shipping product, no distribution. "We had no business, we didn't even have a product," Hassabis said, because the work was on core technology rather than anything sellable.The salary gap did the rest. Hassabis says he was taking nothing while his researchers earned around $100,000 a year and were being offered a hundred times that. "They were getting offers of 10 million a year," he said. If a researcher turned that down, the same companies could return with $50 million. "So at some point, that was going to go wrong."Google's $650 million DeepMind deal, Facebook's rival bid and what Mark Zuckerberg said about the priceGoogle announced the deal in January 2014. The BBC reported a price of about £400 million, making DeepMind Google's largest European acquisition to that point. The figure now generally cited is roughly $650 million. Larry Page's pitch was that Google was already an AI company with the compute and the patience that venture funds could not offer.Facebook had been in talks the year before, and those talks collapsed without a public explanation. Mark Zuckerberg supplied one later. Speaking to South Park Commons, he said Hassabis "totally did a very good job of playing me off of Google to get a good price, which I respect."The sale did not end the argument over control. Sebastian Mallaby's new book on Hassabis details three years of failed negotiations, codenamed Project Mario, in which Hassabis and co-founder Mustafa Suleyman pushed for a semi-independent DeepMind with a nine-seat oversight board. Reid Hoffman offered $1 billion to back a walkout. Sundar Pichai refused to let AI leave Google's core. Hassabis eventually stopped pushing.Twelve years on, the compute question has answered itself. Hassabis runs Google DeepMind, Gemini processes more than 10 billion tokens a minute, and Alphabet has earmarked $175-185 billion in capital expenditure for AI infrastructure in 2026. That is roughly 25 times the sum he once could not raise.
Article Summary: Demis Hassabis sold DeepMind to Google in 2014. He had no product and no revenue when Google, Facebook and Musk started circling. He reckoned that staying in the fight against the biggest technology companies would take roughly $7 billion. Hassabis says he was taking nothing while his researchers earned around $100,000 a year.

Article Title: Read letter that has Satya Nadella, Sundar Pichai, Elon Musk, Jensen Huang, Sam Altman and many other CEOs of biggest American technology companies saying: 'This has our full support'
Article Text:
Arguments for openness

Access : Startups and universities can build on advanced models without prohibitive costs.

: Startups and universities can build on advanced models without prohibitive costs. Competition : Rivalry across developers, chips, and services drives innovation and lowers costs.

: Rivalry across developers, chips, and services drives innovation and lowers costs. Control : Organizations avoid lock-in and retain ownership of their AI capabilities.

: Organizations avoid lock-in and retain ownership of their AI capabilities. Security: Transparency allows vulnerabilities to be identified and remediated across many teams.

Read the letter here

Open Weights and American AI Leadership

July 24, 2026

In the 1980s, early open-source software pioneers challenged the prevailing belief that software would advance only if companies kept tight control over their code. This movement pushed for a transparent ecosystem where developers around the world could study, modify, and improve software. Software developed by the open-source community now supports most of the internet and underlies systems used by the world’s largest technology companies, as well as the U.S. military and federal agencies conducting scientific research, cybersecurity, and other critical missions. Open source did more than lower the cost of software; it created a shared foundation of knowledge on which generations of American engineers and entrepreneurs built their institutional sovereignty.

The United States now faces a similar choice with artificial intelligence. Our AI leadership will be judged not by one frontier AI model, but by whether the United States builds a strong, open ecosystem that diffuses into every sector. This is essential for creating opportunities for innovation and prosperity across the country. It requires expanding access to AI, encouraging competition, robust application layers, and giving Americans greater control over the technology they rely on. Open weight models—AI models that anyone can download, inspect, modify, and run on their own infrastructure—are an important part of that foundation because they make advanced AI more accessible, adaptable, and widely available.

Open weights expand access to the AI economy. Startups, established businesses, universities, and public institutions can build on advanced models without training one from scratch or paying frontier-model prices for every task. Open weights let every organization match the right model to the right job at the right cost, reserving frontier-scale capability for genuine frontier problems and running efficient, specialized models everywhere else. That discipline is what will make AI economically sustainable as its use scales into the billions of everyday tasks. America wins the AI era by diffusing it into the workflows of factories, hospitals, farms, classrooms, and main street businesses.

Open weights also strengthen competition and competition is what keeps the gains of AI broadly shared rather than concentrated in a few hands. By allowing many organizations to build, adapt, and deploy advanced models, open weights create rivalry not only among model developers but across cloud chips, applications, and services. That competition spurs innovation, drives down costs, and distributes the benefits of AI broadly across our economy.

Open weights also give customers greater control. As organizations invest in AI, they want to know that they will not become locked into a single provider or lose the knowledge and capabilities they build over time. Open weight models help provide that assurance by allowing organizations to control their own data, evaluate and adapt models to their own needs, and deploy them wherever their business requirements demand. And as organizations create value with AI, open weights allow them to own that value through self-improving models, specialized capabilities, and accumulated knowledge that drive American sovereignty and prosperity.

To be sure, open weights carry real and distinct risks. Once released, the weights are beyond the original developer’s control, and modified versions are difficult to trace or reverse. But the right response to this risk is not to prohibit open weights. In a world where cybersecurity attackers use advanced AI, defenders need access to models with comparable capabilities so they can detect, simulate, and respond to emerging threats. Open models broaden defensive capability, increase transparency, and allow vulnerabilities to be discovered and remediated across many teams.

In fact, openness may be one of the most important paths to AI safety and security. Relying solely on closed models is not inherently safe: they can be breached, misused, or fail in ways that outsiders cannot detect. And concentrating advanced AI capabilities behind a small number of closed models compounds that risk. It results in a small number of single points of failure, weakens competition, and leaves critical technology in the hands of a few providers. Open weight models, on the other hand, allow a broad community of researchers and developers to examine their behavior, identify vulnerabilities, develop safeguards, and improve them over time. Just as open-source software demonstrated that transparency can be more secure than obscurity, AI safety may depend on giving more people the ability to test and strengthen the models on which society relies. It allows for rigorous benchmarking and evaluation, red teaming, and protections tied to real and demonstrated harms rather than assuming that closed systems are safer by default.

A strong AI ecosystem is not a foregone conclusion. Policymakers have an important opportunity to act. This includes expanding access to compute for startups and researchers, investing in shared training assets (datasets, tools, evaluation frameworks), and keeping the frontier plural by avoiding premature restrictions on open models that stifle competition or drive innovation overseas. These measures must also look at how strong application layers can expand sovereign use of AI across the economy.

In shaping this ecosystem, policymakers should be careful not to conflate legitimate model-development techniques with misappropriation. Distillation, or the practice of using one model’s outputs to help train or improve another, is a widely used technique for model improvement, evaluation, and validation. It reflects a long tradition of learning from, building upon, and improving existing technologies, a tradition that has helped drive innovation since the rise of the open-source software movement. By contrast, unlawful efforts to extract value from closed models raise legitimate concerns. Those concerns should be addressed through targeted legal and commercial frameworks rather than sweeping restrictions on techniques that play an important role in AI innovation.

The age of AI can be one of prosperity. With the right choices, open weight AI can expand opportunity, strengthen competition, extend American technological leadership, mitigate risk, and ensure that the benefits of this extraordinary technology are shared broadly across our economy. That future is worth building, and the United States should lead in building it.

A coalition of 25 leading technology companies and organisations has published a joint letter titled Open Weights and American AI Leadership recently, is urging policymakers to embrace open-weight AI models. The letter argues that America’s AI leadership depends not on a single frontier model but on building a strong, open ecosystem that diffuses across industries. It highlights how open weights AI models that anyone can download, inspect, and run expand access, spur competition, and give greater control to organisations over their data and capabilities. The letter has also drawn endorsements from the biggest names in technology.Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella wrote, “Open-weight models are essential to a healthy AI ecosystem. Together with others across our industry, we are outlining a path for open-weight models to strengthen American competitiveness and expand economic opportunity, while protecting national security,” supporting the letter on X. Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google, posted, “Very happy to support this on behalf of Google. We have long benefited from open source, are big contributors to open source and in fact have consistently made open weights models with Gemma available from @GoogleDeepMind @demishassabis .Onwards!”OpenAI’s Sam Altman also endorsed the letter and wrote on X, “i want the US to win in AI both in open source and proprietary models, and i am glad to see this.” “This has my full support,” added Elon Musk . Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang joined the chorus, highlighting the importance of open-weight AI for startups, researchers, and public institutions and posted on X, “For my first post, I’m sharing a letter @NVIDIA signed on why open models matter. AI will transform every industry, power every company, and be built by every country. Open models strengthen safety and cybersecurity, accelerate innovation and diffusion, and enable sovereignty. The world needs both frontier closed models and frontier open models.”The coalition’s letter outlines several benefits of open weights:
Article Summary: Open Weights and American AI Leadership will be judged by whether the U.S. builds a strong, open ecosystem that diffuses into every sector. It requires expanding access to AI, encouraging competition, robust application layers, and giving Americans greater control over technology they rely on.

Article Title: US government's plans for $100,000 fee on new H-1B work visas rejected by court again; says: Government failed to show that ...
Article Text:
US appeals court keeps lower court ruling in place



US introduced $100K H-1B visa fees in 2025

A federal appeals court has rejected the US government's proposed fees of $100,000 on new H-1B work visas, saying the government failed to show that it was likely to succeed in proving that President Donald Trump had the authority to impose the charge. The ruling keeps in place a lower court's decision blocking the fee that was first introduced in 2025 as part of the Trump administration's broader immigration crackdown. The proposed fee would have sharply increased the cost of hiring highly skilled foreign workers, especially in the technology sector.As stated in a Business Insider report, the 1st US Circuit Court of Appeals in Boston declined to pause a June ruling by US District Judge Leo Sorokin while the Trump administration appeals the case. The decision means the lower court ruling will remain in effect while the legal challenge continues.In his June decision, Judge Sorokin said the proposed fee was effectively a tax, and under the US Constitution, only Congress has the authority to impose taxes."Here, the substance and application of the $100,000 payment reveal that it is a tax, regardless of what the payment is called," Sorokin then wrote.President Trump announced the fee in September 2025, saying the H-1B visa programme had been "deliberately exploited to replace, rather than supplement, American workers with lower-paid, lower-skilled labor."The H-1B programme allows US companies to hire highly skilled foreign professionals in specialised fields such as technology, engineering and healthcare. Each year, the programme issues 65,000 regular H-1B visas, along with 20,000 additional visas for applicants with advanced degrees from US universities.Before the proposed policy, employers typically paid between $2,000 and $5,000 in visa-related fees. According to court filings, demand for new H-1B visas dropped sharply after the administration announced the $100,000 fee. By mid-February, the US Citizenship and Immigration Services had received only a small number of payments under the new policy.
Article Summary: US appeals court keeps lower court ruling in place blocking $100K H-1B visa fees. The fee was first introduced in 2025 as part of the Trump administration's broader immigration crackdown. The proposed fee would have sharply increased the cost of hiring highly skilled foreign workers, especially in the technology sector.

Article Title: China’s biggest memory chip maker CXMT shares jumps 470% after Asia’s biggest IPO
Article Text:
CXMT expands AI and memory chip business

China's biggest memory chip maker, Changxin Technology Group (CXMT), saw its shares jump about 470% on their stock market debut on Monday, July 27 after completing Asia's biggest initial public offering (IPO) this year. The company raised 57.92 billion yuan ($8.6 billion) in the listing before its shares opened at more than 49 yuan, up sharply from the IPO price of 8.66 yuan per share. The strong debut pushed CXMT's market value to around 3.3 trillion yuan, making it the most valuable company listed on China's stock exchanges and highlighting growing investor confidence in the country's semiconductor industry.The Hefei-based company made its debut on Shanghai's technology-focused STAR Market, attracting strong investor interest as China continues to invest heavily in building its domestic semiconductor industry.According to its IPO prospectus, CXMT held a 7.67% share of the global DRAM market in 2025 based on fourth-quarter sales. DRAM, or dynamic random-access memory, is used in products ranging from smartphones and laptops to servers and artificial intelligence systems.The global DRAM market is currently led by Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron Technology, but analysts believe CXMT has the potential to become a much bigger player."I have no doubt the company is going to grow to be a global leader. It's maybe just a question of time that it can be not only a challenger, it can be a global champion in this particular sector," Theodore Shou, CEO of Yiyi Capital, said on CNBC's Squawk Box Asia.The listing also comes weeks after reports that Apple had started testing CXMT's DRAM chips for devices sold in China, drawing more attention to the company's growing role in the semiconductor market.Commenting on the stock's strong first-day performance, Shou said a 470% jump is unusual for a company of CXMT's size."A 470% performance on day one isn't that rare. What's very prominent in this particular case is a company of this size performing so well," he said.He added that the limited number of shares available for trading on the first day, along with strong investor enthusiasm, helped drive the sharp rise.
Article Summary: Changxin Technology Group (CXMT) saw its shares jump about 470% on their stock market debut on Monday, July 27. The company raised 57.92 billion yuan ($8.6 billion) in the listing before its shares opened at more than 49 yuan. The strong debut pushed CXMT's market value to around 3.3 trillion yuan.

Article Title: David Sacks not happy with ‘Chinese’ tag for Open source AI models that Anthropic wants banned
Article Text:
Open source AI is global



Drawing a distinction between AI model



Growing coalition for open-source AI



David Sacks, co-chair of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, has accused AI giant Anthropic of attempting to stifle competition in the AI industry by seeking restrictions on open-source models. According to a report by Benzinga, speaking on the All-In Podcast, Sacks said that labelling Chinese-origin open-source AI models as tainted by intellectual property theft would discourage American developers from building on publicly available models. He also warned that such a move would “put a dagger through the heart of the entire American open source ecosystem,” adding that Anthropic “doesn’t want to have the competition.”Sacks further argued that once model weights are released publicly, they are no longer tied to their country of origin. Developers across the world, including in the US can legally download, modify and also train them on their own infrastructure. He also cited examples such as Mira Murati’s startup Thinking Machines and AI coding startup Cursor, both of which leveraged the open-source Chinese model Kimi K2.5 before further training it with proprietary data.Drawing a distinction between AI model weights and outputs, Sacks said that policymakers often conflate the two. He emphasised that stealing propriety weights would amount to theft, but using outputs to train another system known as distillation is a standard practice. He noted that ChatGPT-maker OpenAI and Claude creator Anthropic themselves have defended training on publicly available content, referencing OpenAI’s legal defense in the New York Times copyright lawsuit.Sacks’ comments come amid a broader push by industry leaders to protect open-weight AI. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang recently endorsed a letter signed by more than 20 companies and organizations — including Meta, Microsoft, IBM, Palantir, Hugging Face, Mistral AI, and Perplexity — urging Washington to embrace open-source models. The letter argued that restricting them would slow innovation, weaken cybersecurity, and limit access for startups, researchers, and public institutions.The coalition defends distillation as a legitimate development method and calls for targeted legal frameworks to address intellectual property concerns rather than broad bans. Sacks echoed this view, urging companies to strengthen safeguards and enforce terms of service instead of pushing for sweeping restrictions that could undermine America’s AI leadership.
Article Summary: David Sacks, co-chair of the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, has accused Anthropic of attempting to stifle competition in the AI industry. Sacks said that labelling Chinese-origin open-source AI models as tainted by intellectual property theft would discourage American developers from building on publicly available models.

Article Title: Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue has 2 demands from OpenAI after Chinese AI model that Sam Altman wants banned saved world’s biggest AI models repository from disaster
Article Text:
Sam Altman

In the spirit of transparency, here’s what I asked @OpenAI:



Why OpenAI’s AI agent hacking shocked the world



Guardrails on ‘western AI’ models fail during emergency response



OpenAI’s ‘late discovery’ sparks federal alert



Days after Sam Altman revealed that OpenAI ’s ‘runaway’ model hacked Hugging Face, the CEO of the world’s largest AI model repository, Clem Delangue, has met with the maker of ChatGPT, and demanded two things in the “spirit of transparency”. In a post shared on X, Delangue asked the leading AI startup to release all the “traces” of the rogue agent for the public and research community to study, and $100 million worth of “compute” to help Hugging Face bolster its cyber defenses.• Radical transparency: let’s release the traces from the “rogue” agents so the entire research community can study what happened.• More capabilities for defenders: let’s commit $100M in compute from OAI to help the Hugging Face community build powerful cyber defenses with the best open and closed models.The first autonomous agent cyberattack is an unprecedented event. It deserves an unprecedented response!A ‘dangerous’ cybersecurity crisis shook the Silicon Valley this week after an autonomous AI agent developed by OpenAI broke free from its testing environment and launched a dayslong cyberattack against open-source AI platform Hugging Face. The incident exposed two uncomfortable truths at once: An autonomous OpenAI ‘on loose’ hacked another system for several days before anyone noticed, and the breach was ultimately contained not by American systems, but by an open-source Chinese AI model that Hugging Face deployed after proprietary Western models failed to respond during the emergency.The incident began around July 9, when an OpenAI agent powered by its GPT-5.6 Sol model and an unreleased, highly capable system escaped its isolated sandbox. Two days later, the rogue agent initiated a multi-day intrusion on Hugging Face’s systems, compromising internal datasets and service credentials before the attack was halted on July 13, as per news agency Reuters.When Hugging Face engineers rushed to respond to the breach, they initially attempted to use leading proprietary US AI models to analyse the threat. However, Western systems – hampered by strict safety guardrails and closed architectures – could not “distinguish an incident responder from an attacker,” leaving security teams unable to contain the attack.Hugging Face turned to GLM 5.2, an open-source model developed by China’s Z.ai lab. It was deployed locally on private servers and successfully analysed over 17,000 attacker footprints to help secure the affected systems. Running locally meant it operated outside the restrictions that hamstrung the Western models, and its open-source architecture gave defenders the flexibility to deploy it on their own terms.The hack has exposed severe gaps in OpenAI’s internal monitoring. According to sources familiar with the investigation, OpenAI failed to realise its own technology was behind the intrusion for over a week. By the time OpenAI officials reached out to Hugging Face around July 20 to report the issue, Hugging Face had already contained the breach with the Chinese model and alerted the FBI. OpenAI publicly acknowledged the event on July 21, calling the escape and subsequent break-in “unprecedented”.“This incident, possibly the first of its kind, proves a point we’ve long believed: AI safety won't be solved by any single company working in secret. It will be solved in the open, collaboratively, with broad access to AI for every defender, everywhere,” said Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue.
Article Summary: Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue met with OpenAI founder Sam Altman and demanded transparency and $100 million in ‘compute’ OpenAI failed to realise its own technology was behind the intrusion for over a week. The breach was ultimately contained not by American systems, but by an open-source Chinese AI model.

Article Title: YouTube will now help creators make thumbnails easily using AI
Article Text:
Custom thumbnails arrive for YouTube Shorts



Generate custom thumbnails with ‘ Ask Studio ’



YouTube has announced a series of updates that are designed to simplify and speed up the thumbnail creation process, giving creators more control over how their content appears across the platform. The video-sharing giant is introducing custom thumbnail options for YouTube Shorts and rolling out conversational AI-generated thumbnails for long-form videos directly within its Studio dashboard.The changes aim to help creators save valuable production time while boosting viewer engagement and click-through rates, the company said in an announcement.In response to one of its most frequently requested features, YouTube said that it is expanding thumbnail customization for its short-form video feed.Custom Shorts uploads: YouTube Partner Program creators can now upload fully custom thumbnail images for their Shorts, offering greater control over branding and visual presentation. The company said that it plans to expand this capability to more creators in the coming months.Desktop frame selection: Creators uploading Shorts via desktop can now choose from three automatically suggested thumbnail frames, matching a feature long available for standard long-form videos.Creators can still select any precise video frame using the YouTube mobile app.For long-form video creators, YouTube is bringing direct thumbnail generation into Ask Studio.Using simple conversational prompts, creators can ask the tool to generate a tailored thumbnail based on their video’s topic. From there, creators can fine-tune specific visual details, such as adjusting colour schemes, shifting layouts, or refining graphic elements by chatting with the assistant.
Article Summary: Custom thumbnail options for YouTube Shorts and conversational AI-generated thumbnails for long-form videos. Changes aim to help creators save valuable production time while boosting viewer engagement and click-through rates. Article Title: Intel rebounds after ‘difficult times’, reports its fastest revenue growth in 15 years
Article Text:
Data center AI and manufacturing drive surge



Intel reported its fastest revenue growth in 15 years, thanks to booming demand for personal computers and artificial intelligence (AI) data center chips. Revenue for the quarter ending in June jumped 25% year-over-year to $16.1 billion – surpassing Wall Street expectations. The chipmaker also projected current-quarter revenue between $15.8 billion and $16.8 billion, signaling continued momentum.“AI is driving unprecedented demand for compute, and as we continue to execute, Intel is well-positioned to capture sustainable growth,” said Intel Chief Executive Lip-Bu Tan, highlighting strength across both chip design and factory operations, as per The Financial Times.The strong performance marks a major comeback for the US chipmaker, which faced severe financial uncertainty just a year ago before receiving strategic backing from the Trump administration in its push to restore domestic semiconductor manufacturing.Intel’s turnaround was powered by a massive spike in demand for central processing units (CPUs), which are increasingly critical for running AI “inference” applications alongside specialised graphics processors (GPUs):While data Center and AI revenue soared 59% to $6.3 billion, well above analyst projections of $5.6 billion; Intel-designed chip sales reached $15.1 billion, beating Wall Street estimates of $13.6 billion.Intel's contract chip manufacturing division generated $5.8 billion, a 31% increase from the prior year. Adjusted net income reached $2.2 billion for the quarter.Under standard GAAP accounting, Intel reported a technical net loss of $11 billion due to accounting volatility tied to escrowed shares from its federal investment deal, which are treated as future obligations.Buoyed by its accelerating growth, Intel raised its 2026 capital expenditure budget from $18 billion to $20 billion and forecast elevated spending through 2027 to outfit its advanced manufacturing facilities.Tan has since secured multibillion-dollar investments from Nvidia and SoftBank, and announced plans to work with Elon Musk on his “Terafab” manufacturing project, all while pursuing company-wide cuts.Intel aims to compete with Nvidia and AMD with its own AI accelerator chip later this year and is seeking to lure big manufacturing clients such as Apple away from TSMC.
Article Summary: Revenue for the quarter ending in June jumped 25% year-over-year to $16.1 billion – surpassing Wall Street expectations. The strong performance marks a major comeback for the US chipmaker, which faced severe financial uncertainty just a year ago.Intel’s turnaround was powered by a massive spike in demand for central processing units (CPUs)

Article Title: Google’s Waymo signals end to Uber deal as companies clash over safety, dirty cars
Article Text:
Waymo's robotaxis carrying passengers in Atlanta, expanding Uber partnership

Waymo-Uber’s ‘blame game’ over routing, dirty cars and bus incidents



Google's sister company and autonomous vehicle unit, Waymo, is reportedly exploring options to exit its partnership with Uber , signaling a deepening rift between the two tech giants as they fight for control over the future of ride-hailing. Citing multiple people familiar with the matter, a report by The Financial Times said that Waymo has held internal discussions about severing its current agreements with Uber, which manages robotaxi rides in major hubs like Austin and Atlanta.The self-driving leader is said to have already notified Uber that it intends to launch its own independent service in those markets starting in January 2028 when its current contract permits.The move marks a shift from 2023, when the companies first joined forces in Phoenix.As Waymo accelerates its expansion across the US, the two companies have increasingly transformed from partners into rivals, with one insider noting they are now “pursuing diverging objectives”, the report said.The relationship has reportedly strained after both companies lodged mutual complaints regarding service quality, safety and operational headaches.While the Alphabet division has questioned the cleanliness and routing of their vehicles and criticised Uber's routing algorithms, Uber has raised issues like bus incidents.In one notable incident in Atlanta, dozens of Waymo vehicles clogged a residential cul-de-sac, which is an issue sources attribute to Uber’s vehicle management. Uber has pushed back, citing unsustainable financial terms and complaining that Waymo's vehicles suddenly go offline during bad weather. In December, Uber formally wrote to Waymo after several robotaxis passed stopped school buses in Austin.The friction has already led to a partial breakup. In May, the two companies allowed their original partnership in Phoenix to lapse.Beyond day-to-day operations, the two companies are locked in a high-stakes lobbying battle to shape state and federal robotaxi laws to benefit their respective business models, The Financial Report said. Uber has lobbied for rules mandating “hybrid networks”, which are platforms that mix human drivers with autonomous cars. In New Jersey, Uber proposed regulations requiring any robotaxi platform to ensure that human drivers fulfill at least 85% of all rides during a three-year pilot program.
Article Summary: Waymo-Uber’s ‘blame game’ over routing, dirty cars and bus incidents has strained the relationship. The two companies are locked in a high-stakes lobbying battle to shape state and federal robotaxi laws to benefit their respective business models.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Bill Gates: Don’t compare yourself with anyone in this world. If you do so, you are insulting yourself
Article Text:
Motivational quote by Bill Gates

What Bill Gates’ quote means

Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates is known for building one of the world’s biggest tech companies, but he’s also known for sharing simple life lessons. One of his most quoted quotes is “Don’t compare yourself with anyone in this world. If you do so, you are insulting yourself." Even years after he first said it, the message continues to connect with people because it speaks about something almost everyone experiences — comparing themselves with others.The quote is a reminder that everyone’s life is different. People grow up in different families, attend different schools, receive different opportunities and face different challenges. That's why comparing your journey to someone else's journey is often unfair.What works for one doesn’t work for another.When Bill Gates said that comparing yourself with others is like "insulting yourself," the tech billionaire is encouraging people to value their own abilities and progress. The quote means one should not decide their own worth by looking at someone else's achievements.In today's world, it is easy to fall into the habit of comparing yourself with others. Social media shows people celebrating promotions, buying homes, travelling to new places or reaching personal goals.At work, people compare salaries and job titles. Students compare exam results, while entrepreneurs compare the success of their businesses. Over time, these comparisons can make people feel that they are falling behind, even when they are making steady progress in their own lives.The quote also highlights that success looks different for everyone. Some people achieve their goals early in life, while others take longer. Some build businesses, others choose careers in science, education, healthcare or public service. There is no single timeline for success, and comparing yourself with someone on a completely different path often creates unnecessary pressure.
Article Summary: Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates is known for sharing simple life lessons. One of his most quoted quotes is “Don’t compare yourself with anyone in this world. If you do so, you are insulting yourself” The quote is a reminder that everyone’s life is different.

Article Title: China's DeepSeek pauses new fundraising days after founder Liang Wenfeng's AI remarks go viral
Article Text:
DeepSeek was founded in 2023

DeepSeek pauses fundraising after founder's reported comments go viral

Chinese artificial intelligence startup DeepSeek has paused its second fundraising round just weeks after raising a record $7 billion, reports Bloomberg citing people familiar with the matter. The move comes days after comments widely attributed to founder Liang Wenfeng about China's AI industry and its competition with the US spread widely online. Prospective investors were verbally informed that they would not be signing investment agreements in the coming days as expected. While the fundraising process has been put on hold for now, discussions remain ongoing and the company could choose to restart the deal at a later stage, the people said.According to people familiar with the discussions, DeepSeek decided to suspend the fundraising partly because Liang was frustrated by online reports about comments attributed to him during meetings with investors in the company's first funding round.Bloomberg News said it has not verified the authenticity of the posts, which reportedly contained a transcript of Liang's meeting with unidentified investors.Chinese media outlets, including Yicai, reported this week that Liang discussed China's continued gap with the US in artificial intelligence and the company's reliance on Nvidia chips for AI development. The company had been seeking to raise at least 10 billion yuan in the second round at a pre-money valuation of at least 480 billion yuan, according to an earlier Bloomberg News report.At the same time, DeepSeek has started preparing for an initial public offering and could file for an IPO as early as this year. Founded in 2023 and owned by hedge fund Zhejiang High-Flyer Asset Management, DeepSeek has become one of China's most closely watched AI startups. Its AI model, launched last year, drew global attention by showing that advanced AI systems could be built using fewer computing resources despite US export restrictions on advanced chips.
Article Summary: DeepSeek pauses fundraising after founder's reported comments go viral. The move comes days after comments widely attributed to founder Liang Wenfeng about China's AI industry and its competition with the US. Prospective investors were verbally informed that they would not be signing investment agreements in the coming days as expected.

Article Title: Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos: "If you double the number of experiments you do per year, you're going to…”
Article Text:
Quote of the day by Jeff Bezos



"If you double the number of experiments you do per year, you're going to double your inventiveness."

Understanding the hidden meaning behind today’s quote



The hidden value of trial and error



Why experimentation matters in everyday life



Lessons hidden inside the quote



Real progress comes from testing ideas, not just planning them.

Practical experiments often uncover insights that are impossible to predict in advance.

Innovation is built through repeated effort over time rather than a single brilliant idea.

The more approaches you explore, the more likely you are to discover effective solutions.

Unsuccessful attempts provide valuable information that guides future improvements.

Trying to eliminate every risk can also eliminate opportunities for meaningful breakthroughs.

Each experiment, whether successful or not, contributes to better decisions and stronger outcomes.

Why the message still feels relevant



Beyond trial and error: Learning with purpose



Innovation is often presented as the result of rare moments of inspiration or breakthrough ideas. Yet people who build successful companies frequently describe it in a far less dramatic way. New products, better systems and unexpected discoveries usually emerge after a long series of attempts, many of which do not work as planned. That pattern can be seen across science, engineering, business and creative work alike. The willingness to try something without knowing the outcome is often what separates steady progress from standing still. Jeff Bezos has spoken about this approach throughout his career, arguing that the volume of experiments matters just as much as the quality of any single idea.At first glance, the statement sounds almost mathematical, but it is not intended as a literal formula. Bezos is pointing towards a simple principle: fresh ideas are usually the result of repeated testing rather than isolated flashes of brilliance.Every experiment produces information. Sometimes that information confirms an idea. Other times it reveals flaws, unexpected customer behaviour or entirely new opportunities.Even unsuccessful attempts contribute to future decisions because they reduce uncertainty. A person or organisation that runs more experiments naturally creates more chances to discover something valuable.The quote also challenges the habit of waiting for certainty before taking action. If every decision has to feel safe before it is tested, the number of experiments remains low, and so does the opportunity to learn.Most innovation follows an uneven path. Early versions of products are refined again and again before they become successful. Scientists test hypotheses that fail. Writers produce drafts that are never published. Engineers discard prototypes that cannot solve the original problem.Each attempt narrows the search for a better solution.This way of thinking changes how failure is viewed. Rather than treating every unsuccessful outcome as wasted effort, experimentation treats it as part of gathering evidence. The important question becomes whether the experiment produced useful knowledge, not simply whether it achieved the desired result.There is also a practical reason for running many small experiments instead of a few large ones. Smaller tests tend to expose problems earlier, allowing adjustments before significant time or money has been invested.Although Bezos made the comment in the context of innovation and business, the underlying idea extends well beyond technology companies.A student preparing for examinations may discover better revision techniques only after trying several study methods. An artist may develop a distinctive style through years of discarded sketches. A chef often refines recipes through repeated adjustments rather than getting everything right on the first attempt.The same pattern appears in everyday problem-solving. People rarely find the most effective approach immediately. They improve by testing different options, observing the results and making gradual changes.Modern workplaces increasingly rely on rapid testing, whether through software updates, product design, marketing campaigns or scientific research. Digital tools have made it easier to gather feedback quickly and adjust ideas before committing to larger changes.The same approach has become common in education, healthcare and public policy, where pilot programmes allow organisations to evaluate new ideas before expanding them. Rather than assuming a single plan is correct, many institutions now rely on evidence gathered through controlled trials and gradual improvements.For individuals, the message remains equally practical. Careers are changing more quickly than in previous decades, making adaptability an important skill. Experimenting with new ways of learning, working or solving problems often provides better guidance than relying solely on prediction.Some people interpret the quote as encouragement to pursue endless ideas without direction.Experiments are most useful when they are deliberate. They begin with a question, test an assumption and produce information that shapes the next decision. Running random trials without reflection does not automatically increase inventiveness.Bezos' observation is less about quantity for its own sake than about creating a habit of continuous learning. More thoughtful experiments expand experience, reduce uncertainty and make genuine innovation more likely over the long term.
Article Summary: Innovation is built through repeated effort over time rather than a single brilliant idea. The willingness to try something without knowing the outcome is often what separates steady progress from standing still. Jeff Bezos argues that the volume of experiments matters just as much as the quality of any single idea.
